title: Kururamma – When God Became a Child
snippet: The human mind finds different ways to relate to the Divine. Some devotees love God as their beloved, some as a friend, and some through the tender affection of a mother...
content:
The human mind finds different ways to relate to the Divine. The beauty of devotion lies in the freedom with which a heart chooses to experience God.

Some devotees love God as their beloved, like the Gopis who adored Krishna. Some serve Him with complete surrender, like Uddhava. Some cherish Him as their closest friend, like Arjuna. And some experience Him through the tender affection of a mother, just as Yashoda loved little Krishna.

We have heard numerous stories about Krishna and His leelas throughout our lifetime. Radhe Radhe... the very words echo thoughts of Krishna and bring His presence closer to our hearts.

Some stories, however, remain with us long after we hear them. One such story was that of Kururamma. I was personally taken aback by her devotion. I carried her name in my thoughts and nurtured a strong desire to visit and experience the land where she had lived with Krishna.

After many years, I was blessed with the opportunity to experience the warmth of that sacred place — Kururamma Sree Krishna Temple, Vengilassery, Thrissur.

Every life on earth goes through its own struggles until self-realisation dawns. It may happen at different stages of life; some may not even reach that understanding in a single birth. Much depends on one's karma and the journey of the soul.

Kururamma, too, had such a journey.

Born as Gauri in 1570 AD, she grew up as an ardent devotee of Lord Krishna. As a child, she was married to an elderly Brahmin Vedic scholar of Kuroor Illam, in Vengilassery village. Unfortunately, she became a widow at the tender age of sixteen, before experiencing the joys of motherhood.

Being part of the Nambudiri community, she was excluded from many social activities and confined largely to the four walls of her home and household responsibilities.

By the grace of God, however, her mind remained deeply absorbed in Krishna. What appeared to be a life of restrictions gradually became a path towards spiritual discovery.

She often observed fasts, and with time, her devotion became the centre of her existence. Her mind gradually detached itself from worldly expectations and turned towards a world filled with Krishna consciousness. Her thoughts, emotions and aspirations began revolving around one presence — Bhagavan Sri Krishna.

However, Gauri's way of life was not understood by her husband's relatives. They began finding fault with almost everything she did. Eventually, they abandoned her and moved into a newly constructed house of their own.

Gauri, however, remained unaffected by these worldly separations.

Her heart gradually expanded beyond her own circumstances. Her eyes would fill with tears of affection at the sight of others. She began looking upon everyone as her own child, extending the tenderness of a mother to all who came her way. In return, people too began to adore her as their own mother.

Thus, Gauri came to be lovingly known as Kururamma.

As the years passed, Kururamma grew older. When even her helping maid had to leave, she found herself increasingly alone. In that solitude, her only prayer was to her beloved Bala Gopala.

*"O my Bala Gopala! I have nobody but You. Please stay with me always. Do not leave me as You did Yashoda."*

Perhaps this was the purest expression of her longing — not the desire for wealth, comfort or recognition, but simply the wish to have her beloved Krishna beside her.

And Bhagavan listened.

Sri Krishna appeared before Kururamma in the form of a little Brahmin boy. Through His Yogamaya, He concealed His divine identity from her.

Kururamma did not see the Supreme Lord in that little boy. She saw only a child who needed her love and care.

Krishna began living with her. He played around the house, accompanied her in her daily activities and helped her with household chores. Like any mischievous little child, He would sometimes trouble her with His playful pranks and even make her angry.

And Kururamma responded just as any mother would — with affection, concern, occasional reprimands and unconditional love.

The Lord of the Universe had willingly become a little child in the home of His devotee, allowing her to experience the motherhood she had never known in her earthly life.
